data.title: On the Conversion of the Bavarians and the Carantanians (9th century)
data.excerpt: The treatise On the Conversion of the Bavarians and the Carantanians (De Conversione Bagoariorum et Carantanorum) was written in 871–873 at the court of Archbishop Adalvín of Salzburg as a response to the Byzantine mission in Great Moravia and Pannonia. It records the church in Nitra, consecrated on Pribina’s estate by Archbishop Adalrám, and gives valuable information on Samo’s Empire, the Principality of Nitra and Pribina’s seat at Blatnohrad.

timeline.description: Archbishop Adalrám of Salzburg consecrated a Christian church on Pribina’s estate in Nitra – the first church in Central Europe attested in writing.

timeline.title: The assembly at Regensburg
timeline.description: King Louis the German handed over to Pribina estates in Pannonia as his own property; the act took place on 12 October 848 in the presence of many bishops and magnates.

timeline.title: Consecrations at Blatnohrad
timeline.description: Archbishop Adalvín celebrated the Nativity of Christ at Koceľ’s fortified seat (Blatnohrad) and consecrated several churches in the surrounding area.

blocks.alt: The treatise On the Conversion of the Bavarians and the Carantanians (9th century)

children.text: The treatise „On the Conversion of the Bavarians and the Carantanians“ (De Conversione Bagoariorum et Carantanorum) was written between 871 and 873 at the court of the Salzburg archbishop Adalvín, as a response to the activity of the Byzantine mission in the territory of Great Moravia and Pannonia and to the work of the Moravian-Pannonian metropolitan Methodius, with the aim of justifying the rights of the archbishopric of Salzburg to the territory of Pannonia. The work extols the merits of the Salzburg archbishops in the Christianisation of the Slavic population living in the territory of Pannonia and condemns the activity of the Byzantine mission in Great Moravia. The treatise contains a mention of the church in Nitra (in 828 the Salzburg archbishop Adalrám consecrated a Christian church on Pribina’s estate in Nitra), which thus became the first church in Central Europe attested in writing. The treatise also contains valuable information on the existence of Samo’s Empire and of the Principality of Nitra, on the expulsion of Pribina from Nitra, on the union of the principalities of Nitra and Moravia, and on the settlement of Pribina and his son Koceľ at Blatnohrad (Transdanubia).
On the Conversion of the Bavarians and the Carantanians – the first written mention of Nitra, Pribina and Blatnohrad

3. Thus far we have spoken of how the Bavarians became Christians, and a list of the bishops and abbots of the diocese of Salzburg has been compiled. Now it must be added how the Slavs called the Carantanians and their neighbours were instructed in the holy faith and how they became Christians, and also how the Huns (Avars) drove the Romans, the Goths and the Gepids out of Lower Pannonia and seized that land. Thereafter the Franks and the Bavarians waged continual wars with the Carantanians, overcame them, and those of them who obediently accepted the faith and had themselves baptised became subjects of the (Frankish) kings. And the land which the rest hold they use to this day in return for payments to the king.

blocks.text:
9. After Archbishop Arn departed from this world, in the year 821 from the birth of the Lord the most pious teacher Adalrám took over the government of the diocese of Salzburg […]
10. After this list of the bishops of Salzburg we shall attempt, for those who wish to learn of it, to make accessible the records as we have found them truthfully set down in the chronicles of the Frankish and Bavarian emperors and kings. When, then, the Emperor Charles had driven off the Huns (Avars) and entrusted episcopal authority over this land to the head of the church of Salzburg, that is to Archbishop Arn and his successors, that they might hold and govern it for all time, both Slavs and Bavarians began to multiply in the land from which the Huns (Avars) had been expelled. In those days the emperor appointed Goteram as the first margrave; he was followed, as the second, by Werinhar, as the third Albrik, as the fourth Gotafrid, as the fifth Gerold. While the said counts had charge of the eastern region, certain (local) dukes also had their seats in those parts subject to the aforesaid episcopal see. Through the said counts they were subordinate to the emperor and were to serve him. Their names were Pribislav, Semikas, Stojmír and Edgar. After them, however, the Bavarian magnates Helmwin, Albgar and Pabo obtained the said territories in possession as counties by donation of the kings. When this had come about, Ratbod took over the protection of the frontiers […]
11. When in the meantime some occasion arose, Pribina then, at the request of the faithful men of the said king, received in fief a certain part of Lower Pannonia around the river called the Sála. Thereupon he settled there and began to build a fortified seat in a certain marshy grove on the bank of the Sála. From all sides he gathered people and increased the number of his subjects. For him (Pribina) Archbishop Adalrám had once consecrated a church on his own estate beyond the Danube, at a place called Nitrava.
12. It thus came to the ears of the most pious King Louis that Pribina had devoted himself to the service of God and of himself, and because many of his faithful men often reminded him of it, he handed over to him (Pribina) in full ownership everything that he had previously held in fief. Excepting, to be sure, those estates which already belonged to the bishopric of Salzburg, to the prince of the apostles Saint Peter and to the blessed Hrodbert, where his body rests and where, as is known, the venerable Archbishop Liupram stands at the head as its administrator. On this basis our liege lord the king decreed that the estates which the said bishop had already acquired in these places, and which may yet be increased by God’s grace, should belong irrevocably, for ever and without any diminution to these places of the aforementioned saints, regardless of the objections and the judicial decision of anyone whatsoever. The following persons were present at this act: Archbishop Liupram, Bishop Erchanbert, Bishop Erchanfrit, Bishop Hartvig, Karloman, Louis, Ernest, Ratbod, Werinhar, Pabo, Fritilo, Tacholf, Deotrich, Waninc, Gerolt, Liutolt, Deotheri, Wolfregi, Jezi, Egilolf, Puopo, Adalprecht, Megingoz, another Adalprecht, Odalrich, Pernger and Managolt. Done at the public assembly in Regensburg in the year of the Lord 848, in the eleventh indiction, on the fourth day before the ides of October (12 October). As long as he (Pribina) lived, he in no way diminished the property of the church, nor did he take anything away from the authority of the said episcopal see. On the contrary, at the urging of the archbishop he strove as far as his strength allowed to increase these estates still further, for after the death of the priest Dominic the priest and excellent teacher Swarnagal was first sent there, together with deacons and clerics, to extend the services of God. After him Liupram then sent there the priest and master of all the arts Altfrid. Him Liupram’s successor Adalvin appointed archpriest there, entrusted him with the keys of the church and charged him to care for all the people in his name. And likewise after his death he appointed Rihpald archpriest. He served here for a longer time, zealously discharging his office by commission of the archbishop. Then, however, a certain Greek named Methodius, after the recent invention of the Slavonic script, disparaging in the manner of philosophers the Latin language, Roman learning and the authoritative Latin script, brought it about that the masses, the gospels and the divine offices performed by those who served them in Latin lost in part their standing with all the people. Since he (Rihpald) could not endure this, he returned to the see of Salzburg.
13. In the year 865 the venerable archbishop of Salzburg Adalvin celebrated the Nativity of Christ at Koceľ’s fortified seat, more recently called Blatnohrad, which had fallen to him (Koceľ) after the death of his father Pribina, killed by the Moravians. And there, on that day, he performed the church services, and on the following day he consecrated a church in honour of Saint Stephen the Protomartyr on an estate belonging to Wittimar. On the day of the kalends of January (1 January) he consecrated, on Koceľ’s estate at Ortahu, a church in honour of Saint Michael the Archangel. In the same year, on the ides of January (13 January), he consecrated at Werid a church in honour of Saint Paul the Apostle. Likewise at that time, 19 days before the kalends of February (14 January), he consecrated at Spizzun a church in honour of Saint Margaret the Virgin. At Termperk he consecrated a church in honour of Saint Lawrence. In the same year he also consecrated a church at Fizkere, and in every church he appointed a priest. Likewise on another occasion, when he came to this land to confirm and to preach, it happened that he found himself at a place called Cella, which belonged to Unzat, where he found a church ready for consecration. He therefore consecrated it in honour of Saint Peter, the prince of the apostles, and appointed a priest of its own there. The church at Stradach he consecrated in honour of Saint Stephen. At Werid, in turn, a church dedicated to Saint Peter, the prince of the apostles, is flourishing. Besides these he consecrated three further churches: one at Quartinaha dedicated to Saint John the Evangelist, a second at Muzziliheschirichun and a third at Ablanza, and to each he appointed a priest of its own.
14. Since the time when, by the decision and command of the lord Emperor Charles, the pontiffs of Salzburg began to govern the people of eastern Pannonia as well, 75 years have passed, during which no bishop other than that of Salzburg had any ecclesiastical authority in this border region. Nor did any priest who had come from elsewhere dare to serve here for longer than three months before he had presented his letter of dismissal to the bishop. This state of affairs was maintained here until the philosopher Methodius began with his new teachings.

children.text: Notes on the persons and dates: Samo – the Frankish king Dagobert reigned from 629 to 639. Adalrám was bishop of Salzburg (821–824) and archbishop (824–836). Ratbod was margrave of the Eastern March from 833 to 854. Mojmír was the first known Moravian prince; he ruled from the mid-820s until 846. Pribina was the first known prince of Nitra; he ruled from the mid-820s until 833 in Nitra and from 840 to 861 at Blatnohrad. Louis the German, king of East Francia, lived c. 805–876. Koceľ, Pribina’s son, was prince of Blatnohrad from 861 to 876. Adalvín was archbishop of Salzburg from 863 to 867 and from 873 to 885. The consecration of the church in Nitra most probably took place in 828.
